newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Cementos Diamante sees boost in profit.
newsitem.headline: Cementos Diamante sees boost in profit.

text.p: Colombian cement maker Cementos Diamante said an expected pick-up in the construction industry later this year should help boost its operating income by more than 30 percent.

"We expect construction to start picking up again by the middle of the year," Diamante president Juan Romero told a news conference. He predicted that this, in turn, would lead to a 5 percent growth in demand for cement over the lackluster levels seen last year.
Diamante is owned by Mexican cement giant Cementos Mexicanos.
Its net profit dropped from 43.5 billion pesos in 1995 to 15.9 billion pesos last year, largely because of costs associated with the takeover of rival Industrias e Inversiones Samper.

But Romero said it was poised to return to solid growth in 1997, including a more than 30 percent rise in operating income, aided in part by cost-cutting measures that will save the company about $55 million per year.
Romero noted that the expansion of the company's Ibague plant in central Tolima province, a project with a $190 million price tag, is due for completion in the first half of 1998.
The project will allow Diamante to boost production to 5 million tonnes a year from its current output of 3.4 million tonnes, he said.

He added that the company was eyeing the possible spin-off of several firms that have nothing to do with the cement industry, including transportation and real estate divisions, but he did not elaborate.
